PASS on the fake backend only (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level); this package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null), no hardware was attached and no hardware or sim-engine run is claimed. The card's entry symbol legged_gym.scripts.sim2sim_zqsa01:run_mujoco exists at legged_gym/scripts/sim2sim_zqsa01.py:105; it takes a TorchScript policy and a Sim2simCfg defined only under __main__, and it imports legged_gym.envs (Isaac Gym), so this package serves the card's models[0], resources/robots/zq_humanoid/urdf/zq_sa01.xml, through MujocoDriver instead of importing or running the upstream script. That is the card's decision (family-config, helper MujocoDriver); there is no deviation from the card. The read-only clone was read in place and no file of it was written by this package. The served model has a free base (7 qpos, 6 qvel) and twelve hinge joints (12 qpos, 12 qvel), so the world state has 19 qpos and 18 qvel values; its twelve motor actuators each carry ctrllimited=true and ctrlrange -200 to 200 (zq_sa01.xml:147-168), and the bridge derives the cap.world.step.v1 ctrl limits from that model range, refusing out-of-range values before writing data.ctrl. cap.world.reset.v1 runs mj_resetData + mj_forward and restores the parsed model qpos0. The served integration step is the MJCF's own 0.002 s (zq_sa01.xml:3). Note that the upstream sim2sim loop overwrites model.opt.timestep with its own 0.001 s dt (sim2sim_zqsa01.py:118,296) and writes PD torques clipped to 200 (sim2sim_zqsa01.py:193-196); this package does not run that loop, so it serves the model's step and takes the caller's control vector. MuJoCo is not installed and cannot be installed here (no network, no pip), so backends['fake'] is the package's stand-in mujoco module in fake.py, declared as the class FakeMujoco. The stand-in parses the same MJCF for the free base, the twelve hinges, the twelve motors, their explicit ctrlranges and the 0.002 s step, but integrates a placeholder velocity proportional to each control value and holds the base fixed; it loads no STL mesh, resolves no contact, inertia, gravity, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics, and does not implement mj_getState/mj_setState. The fidelity gaps list every difference; no trajectory was compared with the real engine. The real mujoco path (a backend name that backends does not list) was not run. WARNINGS kept from the last gate run (all expected, none failed): G6.NOT_RECORDED and G7.UPSTREAM_BACKEND because the fake backend is the package's stand-in for the mujoco library rather than a package class the gate can wrap in a Recorder, so native calls are not recorded and G7 has no fake surface to check; G8.NO_UNIT x3 for the bridge-derived inputs ticks, action.ctrl[*] and seed, which are expected for simulator families. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning was raised. TESTS: test_driver.py keeps the required mhs.testing.check_driver(HERE, backend='fake') call and adds eight cases (model shape from the card model, control-vector length, control-range refusal with zero effect, step advancing the integration state, reset to the model defaults, reset seed recorded without changing the model, published fidelity contract, e-stop latch); they pass. No catalogue_requests: the package uses only cap.world.step.v1 and cap.world.reset.v1. No site-limits.example.json is needed because no operator-required bound and no driver-declared Limit is present; the control envelope is derived from the model at run time.
